verdict.rationale: WorkOS documents M2M applications that issue API access credentials for programmatic, non-human access (workos-docs-32). It also documents custom roles and permissions enforced through session JWTs (workos-docs-22, workos-supp-rbac-jwt), and AuthKit acts as a spec-compatible OAuth authorization server with MCP support (workos-docs-27, workos-docs-8). Together these give a credible base for separate machine identities. However, nothing ties narrowly scoped permissions to M2M credentials, frames them as per-agent identities, or documents instant revocation, and WorkOS's own MCP server acts with the same dashboard access as the human user (workos-docs-52). Missing for 10: per-agent identity provisioning, documented permission scoping on M2M credentials, instant credential or token revocation, and hands-on corroboration.
